description: Portable processor scenarios for OpenAPI decisions sharpened during the 0.2.0 review. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: A later patch-looking OpenAPI edition is refused at load instead of accepted by version-line inference.
A scalar query parameter uses the OpenAPI-declared query location and serialization rather than becoming a body field.
Same-named path and query parameters remain independently writable through the routed source representation retained by revision 6.
Two declared JSON-family request media are preserved as alternatives; the corpus lists both without preference.
An operation with no concrete success-response media omits Accept instead of inventing application/json.
A 201 response uses the default declaration for response media/decode but remains successful because classification is independently 2xx.
The same default declaration may describe a 404 body but never upgrades that non-2xx status into success.
Several effective servers require explicit selection; array order does not create an OpenBindings default.
A header credential colliding with an effective header parameter is refused even when caller input omits the parameter; one artifact declaration never silently supplies the other.
An API-key credential targeting processor-owned Accept cannot replace response-media negotiation and is refused before dispatch.
A request-body schema reached through $ref and allOf is resolved before flattening; its declared property becomes a body field rather than a synthetic body wrapper.
A media type declared for a different success status cannot govern the actual response.
Request-body flattening uses each Media Type Object's own schema: a parameter-colliding candidate is excluded without poisoning a distinct non-colliding artifact alternative.
An OAS header parameter named Authorization is ignored by the artifact's own rule: it creates neither a required input nor a wire header.
Two OAS-distinct header parameters that differ only by case collide on HTTP's case-insensitive field channel and remain unresolvable.
Two content-map keys that differ textually but denote the same parsed media type are a normalized collision, never first-key selection.
A response media declaration with matching parameters outranks its unparameterized sibling while additional actual parameters remain admissible.
Two distinct response declarations tying at the greatest matching parameter specificity are a protocol error rather than content-map order precedence.
A 303 response is not followed by rewriting the artifact-bound POST to GET; it remains the final non-2xx failure response.
The first patch-looking edition beyond the accepted OpenAPI 3.0 set is refused rather than inferred compatible.
An envelope-shaped application object remains ordinary body data because the private routed representation is a structurally disjoint one-tuple.

A location-backed multi-document description resolves an external Path Item and Security Scheme, and fragment-only Parameter, Request Body, and Response references inside the external document stay scoped to that document.
Security Requirement Objects are alternatives: when two complete alternatives are available, invocation selects exactly one and never unions their credentials onto the wire.
Credentials are never volunteered when the effective operation declares no security requirement.
A raw Cookie header parameter cannot coexist with a structured cookie parameter, even when the caller omits both; cookie assembly never silently overwrites an artifact declaration.
An effective Host header parameter cannot replace processor-owned target resolution and is refused before dispatch even when omitted by the caller.
An effective Content-Length header parameter cannot replace processor-owned body framing and is refused before dispatch even when omitted by the caller.
An OAS 3.0 binary schema carries exact raw bytes for a concrete image media type; the lane is schema-driven rather than restricted to application/octet-stream.
A non-canonical Base64 boundary value for an OAS 3.0 raw body refuses before dispatch.
Raw-body bytes are declaration-selected and never sniffed as JSON merely because their decoded spelling is JSON text.
A required raw body with no caller input refuses before dispatch like every other required request body.
An OAS 3.1 schema-omitted image body uses the OpenBindings Base64 boundary and emits raw bytes.
An OAS 3.1 contentEncoding string is transferred as encoded text and is not decoded as OpenBindings boundary Base64.
A required range-only object body challenges for requestMedia during preflight before input consumption and performs zero dispatch; object shape does not imply JSON.
A configured application/json concrete type instantiates a wildcard declaration while the operation input remains a pure application object.
An exact media declaration outranks type and universal ranges for a configured concrete request media type.
A type range outranks a universal range for a configured concrete request media type.
A configured concrete media type covered by a range still refuses when revision 6 defines no encoder for that governing schema and media combination.
A configured text/plain concrete type covered by a wildcard refuses when the governing schema and supplied value are objects.
An optional range-only request body with no caller value bypasses media selection and emits neither a body nor Content-Type.
An optional range-only body supplied without prior requestMedia refuses after input is present rather than issuing an unsafe replay challenge.
An OAS 3.0 binary success response crosses the protocol-independent output boundary as canonical Base64 of its exact octets.
The actual concrete response media selects an OAS 3.1 range, whose schema-omitted body preserves exact bytes as Base64.
A concrete application/json response selected through application/* still emits the parsed JSON application value.
A successful text/event-stream response selected through a declared wildcard retains server-streaming lifecycle and per-event values.
An explicitly dynamic form object rides as one routed application value, preserving a body member independently from a same-named query parameter.
An OAS 3.1 pattern property selects the effective schema and application/json default for its dynamic multipart member.
A declaration-complex exact JSON body rides as one routed application value; no branch or body field is selected by the binding.
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 non-JSON declaration carries request and response octets through the canonical Base64 application boundary.
